item.title: Santa Rosa County Debris Hotline Changes Hours Starting Thursday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County residents seeking help with storm debris removal should note new operating hours for the county's information line, which takes effect Thursday, November 19. The Debris Removal Information Line at 833-495-3919 will operate Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., according to Santa Rosa County Communications. The line will be…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County residents seeking help with storm debris removal should note new operating hours for the county's information line, which takes effect Thursday, November 19.

The Debris Removal Information Line at 833-495-3919 will operate Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., according to Santa Rosa County Communications. The line will be closed for the Thanksgiving holiday on November 26 and 27, with regular hours resuming Monday, November 30.

Residents can call the hotline with questions about proper debris placement, pickup schedules, the overall debris removal process, or to report collection concerns. County officials stress not to call 911 or Emergency Management for debris-related questions — the dedicated line exists specifically for that purpose. As of Tuesday, Santa Rosa County has collected nearly three million cubic yards of debris, with crews expected to continue work for several weeks. The county reminds residents to follow proper placement guidelines to help crews work safely and efficiently.

item.title: Pensacola Beach Holiday Events Set to Launch; Lighted Boat Parade Canceled Due to Hurricane Damage
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce is rolling out a holiday calendar packed with seasonal attractions, though organizers had to cancel one cherished tradition this year. The beloved Lighted Boat Parade won't happen in 2026 because of dock damage from Hurricane Isaias, but the Chamber says it's planning to bring the event back in 2027.…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce is rolling out a holiday calendar packed with seasonal attractions, though organizers had to cancel one cherished tradition this year. The beloved Lighted Boat Parade won't happen in 2026 because of dock damage from Hurricane Isaias, but the Chamber says it's planning to bring the event back in 2027.

Instead, Pensacola Beach is lining up several holiday celebrations starting this month. The Christmas Tree Lighting at the Boardwalk kicks off November 27 with live music from the Bay Bridge Band, photos with Santa, and fireworks at 7 PM. The Surfin' Santa Beach Parade returns December 6 at 2 PM with festive floats and holiday-themed floats, and the Chamber is still accepting parade entries from local businesses and organizations.

Other events include a Holiday Business After Hours sweater party December 8 at Salty Rose, New Year's Eve fireworks at the Soundside at midnight, and the Polar Bear Plunge on January 1 at Paradise Bar & Grill with the theme "Bearly Polar!" according to a Beach Chamber email. The Chamber also is hosting its final Beach Ball Breakfast of 2026 this Friday, featuring a session on year-end business planning.

Vinson's swearing-in marks the transition of the seat after the recent election cycle. The race drew significant attention as a competitive…
item.content:encoded:
Joe Vinson was officially sworn in today as Escambia County's District 4 commissioner following a closely contested election against Republican incumbent Ashlee Hofberger, according to WUWF Public Media.

Vinson's swearing-in marks the transition of the seat after the recent election cycle. The race drew significant attention as a competitive matchup in the county commission elections.

District 4 covers a portion of Escambia County's commission districts. Vinson will now begin his term representing the district's constituents on the five-member Escambia County Commission, which oversees county government operations, budgets, and policy decisions affecting the region.

item.title: UWF student wins silver at national Japanese language competition
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Rosalia Flores, a senior international studies major at the University of West Florida, earned the Silver Award at J.LIVE Talk, one of the nation's most prestigious Japanese language presentation contests, held November 15 in Washington, D.C. Flores competed in the College Category I against finalists from George Washington University and…
item.content:encoded:
Rosalia Flores, a senior international studies major at the University of West Florida, earned the Silver Award at J.LIVE Talk, one of the nation's most prestigious Japanese language presentation contests, held November 15 in Washington, D.C.

Flores competed in the College Category I against finalists from George Washington University and Georgetown University. The competition evaluates participants on the dynamism, vision, and level of engagement of their presentations, focusing on comprehensive communication skills including multimedia and data integration.

Flores faced extraordinary obstacles en route to her achievement. Hurricane Isaias knocked out power and internet service in Pensacola in late October, forcing her to submit her semifinal presentation under difficult conditions. After advancing to the finals, a nationwide FAA ground stop prevented her from traveling to Washington, D.C. The judges accommodated her request to present remotely, and despite these setbacks, she still delivered strongly enough to earn silver.

"Her resilience and positive attitude in overcoming these challenges truly represent the spirit of UWF," said Takami Taylor, senior lecturer of Japanese at UWF's Reubin O'D. Askew Department of Government, who mentored Flores throughout the competition. UWF is the only Florida university to have sent a finalist to J.LIVE Talk twice — in 2021, Ashton Reichard won gold and is now pursuing a master's degree in international affairs.

item.title: Florida submits bid to host U.S. Space Academy at Kennedy Space Center
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida officials announced Tuesday that the state has formally submitted its proposal to NASA to house the new United States Space Academy, with an interim campus planned at the University of Central Florida and a permanent 1,000-acre facility at Kennedy Space Center. According to the Florida Department of Transportation, the proposal aims to…
item.content:encoded:
Florida officials announced Tuesday that the state has formally submitted its proposal to NASA to house the new United States Space Academy, with an interim campus planned at the University of Central Florida and a permanent 1,000-acre facility at Kennedy Space Center.

According to the Florida Department of Transportation, the proposal aims to launch the Academy's inaugural class in fall 2028 at UCF, initially serving 300 students with support from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University. The permanent campus at Kennedy Space Center would accommodate at least 1,200 students by fall 2031, the state said.

Florida's pitch emphasizes the state's existing space infrastructure—including more than $680 million in prior investments—and the concentration of civil, military, and commercial space operations along the Space Coast. Kennedy Space Center, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, and numerous commercial launch companies operate in the region, creating what state officials say is the only location in the nation where all three sectors function at scale in close proximity.

The state proposal also includes creative financing options, with Space Florida potentially using lease-purchase agreements and public-private partnerships to reduce upfront federal costs. Officials say groundbreaking at the permanent Kennedy Space Center site could begin in 2027. Governor Ron DeSantis said Florida's track record in space exploration and innovation makes the state the logical choice to train the next generation of space leaders.

item.title: Senate Aging Committee Examines 'Benefits Cliff' in Work Incentive Hearing
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging will convene Wednesday to examine how safety-net programs may discourage work by imposing sharp income limits — a problem known as the "benefits cliff." The hearing, titled "A Bridge, Not a Barrier: Reforming the Safety Net to Reward Work," will bring together policy researchers and poverty experts to…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging will convene Wednesday to examine how safety-net programs may discourage work by imposing sharp income limits — a problem known as the "benefits cliff." The hearing, titled "A Bridge, Not a Barrier: Reforming the Safety Net to Reward Work," will bring together policy researchers and poverty experts to discuss potential reforms.

Chairman Rick Scott and Ranking Member Kirsten Gillibrand will lead the discussion, which takes place at 3:30 p.m. in Hart Senate Office Building room 216. Scheduled witnesses include Joshua Bandoch, senior vice president of policy research at the Free Enterprise Project and Opportunity Policy Foundation (FREOPP), Greg Lawson of the Buckeye Institute research organization, and Lelaine Bigelow, executive director of Georgetown University's Center on Poverty and Inequality.

The benefits cliff refers to the scenario where recipients of government assistance programs lose eligibility or face reduced benefits as their income rises, potentially creating a disincentive to earn more money or accept better-paying work. The hearing will explore structural changes that could help transition people from government support to self-sufficiency without abruptly cutting them off. A live broadcast will be available through the committee's website.

item.title: Escambia County Hurricane Debris Cleanup Could Cost $80 Million
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The price tag for hurricane debris removal in Escambia County continues to climb, with the final cleanup bill potentially reaching $80 million. County Administrator Wes Moreno provided the updated estimate Tuesday during an interview with Andrew McKay on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola Morning News . The county…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The price tag for hurricane debris removal in Escambia County continues to climb, with the final cleanup bill potentially reaching $80 million.

County Administrator Wes Moreno provided the updated estimate Tuesday during an interview with Andrew McKay on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola Morning News.

The county initially projected cleanup expenses of approximately $64 million, but the massive amount of debris left behind by the hurricane has pushed costs higher.

"We were at, you know, the initial was 64 million," Moreno said. "I think we've surpassed that and we may get as high as 80, so we'll see what it is."

Moreno said crews have already collected more than three million cubic yards of storm debris across Escambia County.

Despite that progress, some neighborhoods are still waiting for their first collection pass.

County officials estimate the first pass is approximately 90 percent complete, with the remaining areas expected to be reached over the next two weeks.

The county is also adjusting contractor assignments to help crews reach neighborhoods where cleanup has lagged.

Although the overall price tag could reach $80 million, Escambia County expects federal disaster assistance to cover most of the expense.

Moreno confirmed that the county's goal is to limit its local share to approximately one-eighth of the total cost.

If the final bill reaches $80 million and reimbursement comes through as anticipated, that would leave the county responsible for approximately $10 million.

The figures remain preliminary, and the final cost will depend on how much debris remains to be collected and the amount of federal reimbursement approved.

item.title: Escambia Sheriff's Office Reduces Hiring Plans Amid Budget Uncertainty
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The Escambia County Sheriff's Office is scaling back its hiring plans as county departments prepare for potential funding reductions tied to Amendment 3. Sheriff Chip Simmons confirmed Tuesday that his department has implemented a modified hiring freeze and postponed a recruit class until January. The department…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The Escambia County Sheriff's Office is scaling back its hiring plans as county departments prepare for potential funding reductions tied to Amendment 3.

Sheriff Chip Simmons confirmed Tuesday that his department has implemented a modified hiring freeze and postponed a recruit class until January.

The department now plans to bring in a smaller group of recruits than originally anticipated.

"We did do what we call a modified hiring freeze. We just pushed it back until January," Simmons told Andrew McKay during an interview on NewsRadio 92.3.

"So we're hiring on a limited basis, only the sworn positions, and we will have a smaller recruit class starting in January."

Simmons said the department is examining potential spending reductions, particularly among positions that do not involve sworn law enforcement officers.

However, he expressed concern about cutting deputies from a department he says is already below average in the number of officers serving per thousand residents.

"There's no celebration for being below average. I certainly am not celebrating that," Simmons said.

The sheriff emphasized that even reductions involving civilian personnel could affect the department's ability to provide services.

He also pointed to recent incidents, including violence at youth football games and a deputy-involved shooting, as examples of the demands already placed on his officers.

Simmons said he expects less money to be available under Amendment 3 but does not believe reductions should come at the expense of sworn law enforcement personnel.

For now, the modified hiring restrictions remain in place, with a smaller recruit class expected to begin in January.

item.title: SS United States Artificial Reef Already Boosting Gulf Coast Dive Bookings
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: DESTIN, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The historic SS United States has barely begun its new life as an artificial reef, but Gulf Coast diving businesses are already reporting a surge in interest. The former ocean liner was intentionally sunk in the Gulf of Mexico last week, becoming the world's largest artificial reef. Now, local dive charter operators…
item.content:encoded:
DESTIN, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The historic SS United States has barely begun its new life as an artificial reef, but Gulf Coast diving businesses are already reporting a surge in interest.

The former ocean liner was intentionally sunk in the Gulf of Mexico last week, becoming the world's largest artificial reef.

Now, local dive charter operators say the massive underwater attraction is bringing new customers to Northwest Florida during what would normally be a slower time of year.

Captain Andy Ross of Niuhi Dive Charter told WEAR-TV that demand increased dramatically after he posted photographs from an early trip to the wreck.

"Our booking rate has just shot through the roof," Ross told Channel 3.

Ross said his business has received approximately 30 calls a day, with customers booking trips months ahead.

"We're booking at this time of the year when normally we're slowing down and we're not doing much. We're slam busy," Ross said.

The SS United States joins another famous artificial reef in Northwest Florida: the former aircraft carrier USS Oriskany, which was sunk off Pensacola in 2006.

Kerry Freeman, owner of Pensacola-based Dive Pros, believes having both wrecks in the region will create lasting economic benefits.

"When we got the Oriskany, it was a grand jewel in our crown of diving attractions. So now we have two grand jewels in our crown," Freeman told Channel 3.

Freeman expects the new reef to attract visitors from across the United States and overseas, benefiting dive shops, charter operators, restaurants and hotels.

The nearly 1,000-foot ocean liner rests upright on the Gulf floor, with its upper structure approximately 65 feet below the surface and its deepest portions reaching about 180 feet.

That range of depths provides opportunities for different levels of diving experience, although deeper sections require advanced technical training.

The project was led by Okaloosa County, with support from regional tourism partners, including Escambia County.

The SS United States was once America's most celebrated passenger liner and still holds the transatlantic speed record for an ocean liner.

Its transformation into an artificial reef is expected to create new marine habitat while bringing additional recreational diving tourism to the Gulf Coast.

item.title: Escambia County Schools Show Mixed Results on State Assessments
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County schools are reporting some progress on student performance, with fewer pupils landing in the lowest achievement levels, according to Citizen Portal News Florida. However, the district continues to trail state averages in key subjects including English language arts and mathematics, suggesting persistent challenges in core academic…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County schools are reporting some progress on student performance, with fewer pupils landing in the lowest achievement levels, according to Citizen Portal News Florida. However, the district continues to trail state averages in key subjects including English language arts and mathematics, suggesting persistent challenges in core academic areas.

The improvement in moving students out of the lowest performance tiers represents a step forward for the district, but educators and administrators will likely need to focus additional resources and intervention strategies on math and reading instruction to close the gap with state performance benchmarks.

This mixed picture reflects trends seen in many Florida school districts as they work to boost student achievement across all demographic groups. The data underscores the ongoing need for targeted academic support in Escambia County classrooms.

The new routes will connect the coastal Alabama airport to Wichita, Kansas; Indianapolis, Indiana; Little Rock, Arkansas; Shreveport, Louisiana; and Minneapolis, Minnesota. The…
item.content:encoded:
Gulf Shores International Airport is expanding its flight network with five new nonstop destinations, according to an announcement posted to the airport's Facebook page.

The new routes will connect the coastal Alabama airport to Wichita, Kansas; Indianapolis, Indiana; Little Rock, Arkansas; Shreveport, Louisiana; and Minneapolis, Minnesota. The expansion marks a significant boost to air travel options from the Gulf Shores market.

The announcement comes as regional airports across the Southeast continue to add capacity and routes to meet growing travel demand. Gulf Shores, located about 60 miles south of Pensacola, serves as an alternative airport option for Northwest Florida travelers.

item.title: Florida Vibe Welcome Draws Hundreds as Pensacola Prepares for Professional Softball
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Professional women's softball is coming to Pensacola, and the community is already showing its enthusiasm. Hundreds of people gathered at Blue Wahoos Stadium Monday evening to welcome the Florida Vibe, the city's newest professional sports franchise. The team will begin playing home games at Blue Wahoos Stadium in…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Professional women's softball is coming to Pensacola, and the community is already showing its enthusiasm.

Hundreds of people gathered at Blue Wahoos Stadium Monday evening to welcome the Florida Vibe, the city's newest professional sports franchise.

The team will begin playing home games at Blue Wahoos Stadium in 2027 as part of the six-team Professional Softball League.

Community investor Quint Studer, who helped bring the franchise to Pensacola, told NewsRadio 92.3 he was surprised by the turnout.

"I was stunned. I bet you we have 500 people here. I mean, that's amazing," Studer said during an interview at the stadium.

Studer believes the addition of professional women's softball will have a lasting impact on local girls who aspire to compete at higher levels.

"Girls have always wanted to play sports, but they're following guys. Now they can see women being professionals, and I think it's just great role models for them," he said.

Ryan Moore, former owner of the Florida Vibe and owner of the Professional Softball League, said the upcoming season will feature six teams playing a 40-game schedule.

Each franchise will play 20 games at home and 20 on the road, with a league championship planned for mid-August.

In addition to Pensacola, Studer identified Atlanta, Birmingham, Knoxville, St. Louis and Kansas City as the league's other markets.

The Florida Vibe will share Blue Wahoos Stadium with Pensacola's minor league baseball team, with softball games scheduled around the baseball season.

Studer said he expects the players to become active members of the Pensacola community, participating in events and connecting with local young athletes.

The team's arrival adds another professional sports attraction to downtown Pensacola and creates new opportunities for local softball fans to watch professional women's competition.

item.title: Escambia County Reassigns Debris Collection Territory as Residents Question Cleanup Map
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County is changing how hurricane debris collection crews are deployed as residents in several neighborhoods continue waiting for their first pickup. County Administrator Wes Moreno confirmed Tuesday that part of the territory previously assigned to Panhandle Paving has been reassigned to another cleanup…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County is changing how hurricane debris collection crews are deployed as residents in several neighborhoods continue waiting for their first pickup.

County Administrator Wes Moreno confirmed Tuesday that part of the territory previously assigned to Panhandle Paving has been reassigned to another cleanup contractor.

The adjustment affects portions of the county around Johnson Street and Olive Road, where some residents have reported lengthy delays.

"What we've done is we've taken a piece of the geography that Panhandle had, and we've given a little bit more of a piece to Ashbrook to help expedite things and get the debris picked up a little quicker," Moreno told Andrew McKay on NewsRadio 92.3.

The contractor's name appears as "Ashbrook" in the interview transcript and should be checked against the county's records before publication.

Moreno said the county has collected more than three million cubic yards of debris and estimates that approximately 90 percent of the first collection pass has been completed.

He hopes the remaining neighborhoods will receive their first pickup within the next two weeks.

Moreno also acknowledged concerns about the county's online debris tracking dashboard.

Residents have complained that some areas appear to be marked as having received their first collection pass even though debris remains untouched along individual streets.

"I'll be honest with you, Andrew. I haven't liked that dashboard since we put it up," Moreno said.

"It's only as good as the information that gets entered into it."

Moreno said a consultant is responsible for maintaining the information displayed on the dashboard.

The county has also begun moving toward debris collection in gated subdivisions, which requires additional authorization.

Residents with questions about collection routes can contact the county's debris information line at 850-332-1226.

item.title: Pensacola Mardi Gras hosts final city meeting Thursday; Krewes to learn Fat Tuesday room assignments

Doors open at 5 p.m., with the meeting beginning at 6 p.m. The free, public gathering is the last chance for Krewes, businesses, and the community to connect before the season officially kicks off…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Mardi Gras will hold its second and final city-wide meeting of the 2027 season Thursday, November 19, at Apple Annie's inside Seville Quarter. Doors open at 5 p.m., with the meeting beginning at 6 p.m. The free, public gathering is the last chance for Krewes, businesses, and the community to connect before the season officially kicks off January 2.

The highlight of Thursday's meeting will be the official room selection for Fat Tuesday, where 12 Krewes will learn which of seven available rooms they'll host and decorate inside Seville Quarter on February 9. Some rooms will be shared among multiple Krewes. To participate in the selection, Krewe leaders must attend the meeting and have completed the Krewe Information Jotform, which was distributed via email.

The 2027 Mardi Gras season runs through Fat Tuesday on February 9 and includes the January 2 Kick-Off Celebration, Second Line Tuesdays from January 5 through February 2, parade week events February 4-7, and the final Fat Tuesday celebration at Seville Quarter. PMG President Danny Zimmern and other Krewe leaders and organizers will discuss their plans for the season. For more information, visit pensacolamardigras.com.
